title: Predictive Techniques for Stock Price Movement Using Quantum-Classical Approach: A Comprehensive Review
journal_or_venue: International Journal of Science, Engineering and Technology
abstract_summary: This review surveys quantum-classical hybrid approaches for predicting stock price movement, focusing on quantum feature maps, variational quantum circuits, and hybrid architectures that combine classical preprocessing with quantum modeling. It assesses potential benefits (richer feature encoding and possible computational speedups), summarizes case studies and current limitations (hardware noise, data encoding challenges, algorithm maturity), and outlines directions for future research.
methodology_description: This paper is a qualitative literature review and conceptual design study. The authors surveyed recent literature (citations provided) on quantum computing and quantum-classical hybrid methods as applied to financial forecasting and stock price movement. They synthesized key concepts (qubits, superposition, entanglement), categorized quantum machine learning approaches into four quadrants (CC, CQ, QC, QQ), and reviewed building blocks such as quantum feature maps (angle/amplitude/data encoding), variational quantum circuits (VQCs), and hybrid architectures. The review collates reported applications and case studies (e.g., QSVM, QNN, QLSTM, quantum annealing for feature selection), summarizes reported benefits and limitations (hardware constraints, algorithm development, data preparation, interpretability), and identifies future research directions (algorithmic improvements, error correction, hybrid designs). Based on the literature synthesis, the authors propose a logical multi-layer hybrid quantum-classical architecture (Input layer, Classical ML layer, Quantum layer, Output layer) for stock price prediction. The manuscript does not report original experimental work, benchmarking experiments, or new datasets; it is conceptual and survey-oriented.

results_summary: This review surveys quantum-classical hybrid approaches for stock price prediction and finds a mixed picture: classical ML methods (LSTM, RF, DNN, etc.) already achieve high accuracy on many benchmark or curated datasets, and quantum-inspired or quantum-hybrid methods show promise in simulation (some reported percent-level improvements). Key quantum building blocks include quantum feature maps, variational quantum circuits, and hybrid pipelines where classical preprocessing feeds quantum models. However, practical quantum advantage has not been demonstrated on current noisy hardware — simulator gains often disappear on real devices due to noise and limited qubit counts. The field faces hardware, algorithmic, data-encoding, and interpretability challenges; research directions include designing more robust quantum algorithms, better hybrid architectures, and leveraging advances in error correction and logical qubits.
performance_claims: A hybrid PRE + DNN classical model produced a ~5% increase in accuracy (citation [5]).
A Random Forest with a modified investment strategy achieved ~91.27% accuracy (citation [6]).
An LSTM combined with technical indicators (RSI, MACD, SMA) achieved 93% accuracy for selected Vietnamese stocks (citation [7]).

A hybrid Quantum LSTM (QLSTM) showed about a 9% prediction accuracy improvement in a simulated noiseless environment versus classical LSTM, but this advantage disappeared on actual quantum hardware (citation [13]).

The authors anticipate a 'near quadratic' speed-up using quantum Monte Carlo simulation techniques for some financial computations (citation [8]) (presented as a motivation rather than demonstrated result).
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper presents potential quantum advantages (speedups and improved accuracy) and cites simulation studies that report gains, but it acknowledges that these improvements have not been reliably reproduced on current noisy quantum hardware. Thus quantum advantage is described as plausible and actively researched but not demonstrated in practical, real-world financial prediction tasks.

contradictions: Some studies report simulation-level accuracy gains for quantum/hybrid models (e.g., a ~9% improvement for QLSTM in noiseless simulation), but the review notes these gains have not been replicated on current noisy hardware and may not generalize — a direct contradiction between simulated claims and hardware reality (see cited simulation claims vs. hardware limitations discussion).

The authors speculate possible near-quadratic speed-ups from quantum Monte Carlo/quantum subroutines, yet repeatedly highlight hardware qubit-count limits, noise, and immature algorithms that preclude scaling to real-world financial datasets today, contradicting unqualified claims of near-term scalability.

While some cited works claim quantum/hybrid models outperform classical baselines on specific curated datasets (citations [5],[6],[7] referenced for accuracy numbers), the review stresses that classical ML methods (LSTM, RF, DNN) already achieve high accuracy on many benchmarks, calling into question general claims of quantum superiority across diverse, real-world datasets.
